mainTopic: No מלקות for a לאו with no action, the prohibition against vowing by or mentioning idols, the permission to mock עבודה זרה, and why ישראל worshipped idols.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about leftover פסח meat. רבי יהודה and רבי יעקב both say there is no מלקות, but they give different reasons, and the גמרא infers that רבי יהודה gives מלקות even for a לאו with no action. Next the גמרא finds the source that vowing or swearing in an idol's name is forbidden: 'לֹא יִשָּׁמַע עַל פִּיךָ' in שמות. That source also forbids causing others to swear by an idol, which supports אבוה דשמואל's ban on going into a partnership with a נכרי. A story about עולא staying in קלנבו teaches רבי יוחנן's rule that an idol whose name is written in תנ״ך may be mentioned. רב נחמן then rules that mocking עבודה זרה is the one kind of mockery that is allowed. The גמרא brings פסוקים and explanations that make idols look foolish: pocket idols, calves that are kissed, idols shaped like animals, and חזקיה saved from the fire. Finally, רב says ישראל knew idols were empty and worshipped them only to permit עריות. The גמרא defends this against a challenge and begins a story about אליהו and a starving child, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No lashes for leftover פסח meat, says רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends רבי יהודה's view. Because the תורה added a positive command (burn the leftovers), there is no מלקות for leaving meat over.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The verse came to give a positive command after the prohibition] to say that one is not flogged for it. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining a ברייתא in the middle. רבי יהודה is explaining why someone who leaves over פסח meat does not get מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה first says not to leave the meat over, and then says to burn whatever is left. רבי יהודה reads that second command as the fix for breaking the first one. A לאו that has a built-in fix like this does not carry מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: To say / to teach. The verse comes to teach this point.
A prohibition that has a positive command to fix it. This is the idea behind רבי יהודה's reason.

phrases.english: to say that one is not flogged for it,
phrases.notes: We're starting mid-sentence. The פסוק is שמות 12:10: don't leave meat over until morning, and burn whatever is left.

phrases.english: the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵין לוֹקִין עָלָיו, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא that the גמרא brought just before this point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, there is no מלקות for leaving over פסח meat, because the תורה gave a positive command (burning) to fix it.

steps.title: רבי יעקב gives a different reason: no action was done
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב agrees there is no מלקות, but says the reason is that leaving meat over is a לאו שאין בו מעשה, and no לאו like that brings מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב says: That is not the reason. Rather, it is because it is a prohibition with no action, and for any prohibition with no action, one is not flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב agrees with the outcome, no מלקות, but gives a different reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving meat over means doing nothing; you simply fail to eat it in time. רבי יעקב says that kind of passive sin never brings מלקות. This is a different rule from רבי יהודה's rule about a positive command fixing the לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: That's not the reason. Literally, "this is not from that name."
A prohibition that is broken without doing any physical action.

steps.confusionAlert: Both רבי יהודה and רבי יעקב say there is no מלקות here. They argue only about WHY. That difference in reasoning is what the גמרא builds on in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov says:
This is not for that reason,
phrases.notes: Literally "not from this name." He means: that's not why there are no lashes.

phrases.english: rather, it is because it is
a prohibition that has no action in it,
and any prohibition that has no action in it,
one is not flogged for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִן הַשֵּׁם הוּא זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's reason and puts a different one in its place, while keeping the same outcome.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יעקב, no לאו שאין בו מעשה brings מלקות, and leftover meat is such a לאו.

steps.title: So רבי יהודה must hold lashes are given even with no action
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that רבי יהודה needed a special reason here. That means that in general he holds there is מלקות for a לאו שאין בו מעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: By inference, רבי יהודה holds: one is flogged for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the argument it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהודה agreed that no-action sins never bring מלקות, he would not need the special "positive command" reason. Since he looked for a different reason, he must hold that a לאו שאין בו מעשה normally does bring מלקות. That would include vowing or swearing in an idol's name.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference. Literally, "from the general meaning" of what was said.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, a person can get מלקות even for a לאו with no action. רבי יעקב says no.
steps.whyThisMatters: Vowing or swearing in an idol's name is done with speech alone, with no action. So this inference tells us that according to רבי יהודה, a person can get מלקות for it.

phrases.english: By inference, Rabbi Yehuda holds:
one is flogged for it.
phrases.notes: "It" means a prohibition with no action in general, not the leftover meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the difference between the two reasons in steps 1 and 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה holds there is מלקות for a לאו שאין בו מעשה.

steps.title: The משנה: vowing or swearing in an idol's name is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line of the משנה that says vowing or swearing in an idol's name breaks a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who vows in its name and one who swears in its name breaks a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new piece of the משנה and quotes it. This is a setup for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "In its name" means in the name of an idol. The משנה says both making a vow and confirming something with an oath in that name are forbidden by a לאו. The משנה does not say where in the תורה that לאו comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: One who confirms (his words) with an oath.
In its name, meaning the idol's name.

phrases.english: One who vows in its name and one who affirms in its name,
phrases.notes: "Its name" is the name of an idol. "Affirms" means backing up his words with an oath.

phrases.english: this one is in violation of a prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַנּוֹדֵר בִּשְׁמוֹ וְהַמְקַיֵּים בִּשְׁמוֹ, הֲרֵי זֶה בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vowing or swearing in the name of an idol breaks a לא תעשה.

steps.title: Where do we learn this prohibition from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the פסוק that forbids vowing or swearing in an idol's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who vows in its name and one who swears in its name: from where do we derive this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the משנה's case and asks for its source in the תורה. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated the rule but gave no source. Before the גמרא accepts that this is a real לאו, it wants to find the פסוק behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this? A short form of מִנַּיִן לָנוּ.

phrases.english: One who vows in its name and one who affirms in its name,
from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's rule that was just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that vowing or swearing in an idol's name is a לאו.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives the source: do not mention, vow, or swear by an idol
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that reads the פסוק in שמות as forbidding a person to mention an idol, to vow or swear in its name, or to cause others to do so.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And the name of other gods you shall not mention' means a person should not say to his friend, 'Wait for me next to such-and-such idol.' 'It shall not be heard on your mouth' means he should not vow or swear in its name, and he should not cause others to vow or swear in its name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 5 by quoting a ברייתא that explains the פסוק in שמות 23:13 line by line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק, 'do not mention,' forbids even a casual mention of an idol, such as using it as a meeting place. The second half, 'it shall not be heard on your mouth,' is the source for the משנה's rule against vowing or swearing in an idol's name. It also forbids causing someone else to vow or swear by an idol.

keyTerms.meaning: It shall not be heard on your mouth
He will confirm a statement with an oath
He will cause (someone else to do something)

steps.confusionAlert: The two halves of the פסוק teach two different things. 'Do not mention' covers even a casual mention, like naming an idol as a meeting place. 'It shall not be heard on your mouth' is the part about vows and oaths.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source for the לא תעשה that the משנה mentioned in step 4.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
"And the name of other gods you shall not mention" –
phrases.notes: שמות 23:13

phrases.english: that a person should not say to his friend
"Wait for me next to such-and-such idol."
"It shall not be heard on your mouth" –
that he should not vow in its name
and should not confirm a statement in its name,
phrases.notes: To 'confirm' here means to back up what you say with an oath.

phrases.english: and should not cause others
to vow in its name or to confirm with an oath in its name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 by giving the פסוק and how a ברייתא reads it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is 'לֹא יִשָּׁמַע עַל פִּיךָ' in שמות 23:13. It forbids vowing or swearing in an idol's name and causing others to do so.

steps.title: A second reading: the פסוק warns the מסית and the מדיח
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא offers another way to read 'לֹא יִשָּׁמַע עַל פִּיךָ': it is the warning (אזהרה) against the מסית and the מדיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'It shall not be heard on your mouth' is a warning against the מסית and against the מדיח.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second, different reading of the same words of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, 'heard on your mouth' means a person should not use his mouth to talk others into idol worship. The מסית persuades individuals, and the מדיח leads a whole city astray. The פסוק would serve as the אזהרה, the warning that a punishment needs.

keyTerms.meaning: A warning; the לאו that forbids an act which has a punishment
One who persuades individuals to worship idols
One who leads a whole city to worship idols

phrases.english: Another explanation:
"It shall not be heard on your mouth" –
is a warning against the inciter and the one who leads a city astray.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reading of the same פסוק that step 6 explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לֹא יִשָּׁמַע עַל פִּיךָ' is the אזהרה for the מסית and the מדיח.

steps.title: The מסית already has his own פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second reading: the warning against a מסית is already written clearly elsewhere, so this פסוק is not needed for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מסית? It is written explicitly about him: 'And all Israel shall hear and fear, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this פסוק would be needed for the מסית, when a different פסוק already warns against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים 13:12 says that everyone will hear about the מסית's punishment and be afraid to do the same. That already works as a warning against inciting, so a second source for the מסית would be extra.

keyTerms.meaning: They will hear and be afraid

phrases.english: An inciter? It is written explicitly about him:
"And all Israel shall hear and fear, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 13:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 7 that the פסוק is the warning for the מסית.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'לֹא יִשָּׁמַע עַל פִּיךָ' is the אזהרה for the מסית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מסית already has an explicit warning in דברים 13:12, so this פסוק would be extra for him.

steps.title: Rather, the פסוק is the warning for the מדיח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the second reading: 'לֹא יִשָּׁמַע עַל פִּיךָ' is the warning only for the מדיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a warning against the מדיח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the second reading so that the פסוק applies only to the מדיח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מסית already has his own warning, but the מדיח does not have a clear one anywhere else. So this פסוק fills that gap and serves as the מדיח's אזהרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; this replaces the earlier idea

steps.whatToRemember: In the second reading, 'לֹא יִשָּׁמַע עַל פִּיךָ' is the warning for the מדיח only, because the מסית already has his own פסוק.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a warning against the one who leads a city astray.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 by limiting the פסוק to the מדיח.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק warns both the מסית and the מדיח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק warns only the מדיח, because the מסית already has his own warning.

steps.title: The ברייתא's rule on causing others supports אבוה דשמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's line that one may not cause others to vow or swear by an idol, and says this supports אבוה דשמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he should not cause others to vow in its name or swear in its name.' This supports the father of שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes again the ברייתא's line about causing others to vow or swear, so it can use it as support for an אמורא. It is setting up the statement of אבוה דשמואל that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids not only swearing by an idol yourself but also causing someone else to do it. That is exactly the idea behind אבוה דשמואל's rule, so the ברייתא backs him up.

phrases.english: "And he should not cause others
phrases.notes: The גמרא is going back to the last line of the ברייתא from step 6.

phrases.english: to vow in its name or to confirm with an oath in its name."
This supports the father of שמואל,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the מסית/מדיח discussion and returns to the first reading of the ברייתא from step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The view of אבוה דשמואל that one may not go into a partnership with a נכרי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's line that one may not cause others to vow or swear in an idol's name.

steps.title: אבוה דשמואל forbids a partnership with a נכרי
steps.stepSummary: אבוה דשמואל rules that a Jew may not go into a partnership with a נכרי, because the נכרי may end up swearing to him by his idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the father of שמואל said: A person may not make a partnership with a נכרי. The נכרי might come to owe him an oath and swear by his idol, and the תורה said, 'It shall not be heard on your mouth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the actual statement of אבוה דשמואל that the ברייתא supports.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a partnership, a dispute could lead to the נכרי owing his Jewish partner an oath. He would swear by his own idol, so the Jew would have caused an oath in an idol's name. That falls under 'לֹא יִשָּׁמַע עַל פִּיךָ,' just as the ברייתא taught.

keyTerms.meaning: He will come to owe him an oath

steps.confusionAlert: The Jew does not swear here; the נכרי does. The איסור is that the Jew caused the oath by an idol, which is the 'causing others' rule from the ברייתא.
steps.whatToRemember: 'לֹא יִשָּׁמַע עַל פִּיךָ' forbids vowing or swearing by an idol and also causing someone else to do it. That is why אבוה דשמואל forbids a partnership with a נכרי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This takes the ברייתא's rule into a practical business question: avoiding a situation that could lead a non-Jew to swear by his idol.

phrases.english: for the father of שמואל said:
It is forbidden for a person
to make a partnership with a non-Jew,
lest he come to owe him an oath
phrases.notes: 'He' is the non-Jewish partner, who might owe the Jew an oath.

phrases.english: and he swears by his idol,
and the Torah said: "It shall not be heard on your mouth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the statement of אבוה דשמואל that step 10 said the ברייתא supports.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew may not go into a partnership with a נכרי, so as not to cause the נכרי to swear by his idol.

steps.title: עולא stays overnight in קלנבו
steps.stepSummary: A short story: עולא lodged in קלנבו, and when רבא asked where he stayed, עולא said the name out loud.
steps.simpleTranslation: When עולא came, he stayed overnight in קלנבו. רבא asked him: Where did the master stay? He answered: In קלנבו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that sets up the next move. עולא says the name of a place that contains the name of an idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The place name קלנבו includes the name נבו, which is an idol. By saying the name out loud, עולא seems to be mentioning an idol's name. This sets up רבא's challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A place name that contains the name of the idol נבו
Master, a respectful way to address a sage

phrases.english: When עולא came,
phrases.notes: He came from ארץ ישראל to בבל.

phrases.english: he stayed overnight in קלנבו.
phrases.notes: Look at the end of the name: נבו is the name of an idol.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: וְהֵיכָא בָּת מָר?
phrases.english: רבא said to him: And where did the master stay overnight?
He said to him: In קלנבו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about mentioning idol names. It is related to the earlier steps about idols, but it is a new story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup story: עולא said the name קלנבו, which contains the idol's name נבו.

steps.title: רבא objects: we may not mention other gods
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges עולא: the תורה forbids mentioning the names of other gods, so how could he say קלנבו?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But it is written, 'And the name of other gods you shall not mention'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges עולא for saying a name that contains an idol's name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to forbid saying any idol's name at all. Since קלנבו contains נבו, saying it looks like breaking this rule. So עולא needs to explain why it was allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it not written? This opens a challenge from a פסוק

phrases.english: He said to him: But is it not written:
"And the name of other gods you shall not mention"?
phrases.notes: שמות 23:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's action from step 12.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק forbids mentioning an idol's name, and קלנבו contains the idol's name נבו.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: idols written in the תורה may be named
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers with רבי יוחנן's rule: if an idol's name is written in the תורה, it is permitted to say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן said: Any idol that is written in the תורה, it is permitted to mention its name.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא defends himself by quoting a rule from רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on mentioning idols does not cover names that already appear in the holy text. Since we say those names anyway when we read the פסוקים, saying them in everyday speech is allowed too. Now the only open question is whether נבו is really written.

keyTerms.meaning: That is written in the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: Here תורה means all of תנ״ך, not just the חומש. The proof in step 16 comes from ישעיהו.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן said:
Any idol that is written in the Torah –
it is permitted to mention its name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the prohibition: names written in the Torah are excluded.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every idol's name is forbidden to mention.
steps.terutzMaskana: An idol whose name is written in the Torah may be mentioned.

steps.title: Where is this idol written?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks where the idol נבו is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where is this one written?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא accepts the rule but asks for the source. Where does נבו appear in a פסוק?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's rule only helps עולא if נבו is actually written somewhere. So רבא asks for the exact place.

phrases.english: And this one, where is it written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source that applies step 14's rule to נבו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where the idol נבו appears in the פסוקים

steps.title: נבו is written in ישעיהו
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers with the פסוק 'בל bows down, נבו stoops.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'בל bows down, נבו stoops.'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא shows that נבו appears in a פסוק, so its name may be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because נבו is named in ישעיהו, it falls under רבי יוחנן's rule. Saying קלנבו was therefore allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of an idol mentioned in ישעיהו

phrases.english: As it is written:
"Bel bows down, נבו stoops."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 46:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נבו is written in ישעיהו 46:1, so it may be mentioned.

steps.title: רב משרשיא: a משנה names the idol גדיון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether unwritten idol names are really forbidden, and רב משרשיא challenges from a משנה that mentions גדיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is not written, is it forbidden? רב משרשיא objected: If a man saw one discharge as long as three, like the time from גדיון to שילה, which is the time of two immersions and two dryings, he is a full זב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the flip side of רבי יוחנן's rule. A משנה casually names the idol גדיון, which seems not to be written anywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only written idol names may be said, then the תנא of the משנה should not have said גדיון. The משנה uses it as an ordinary distance marker. That suggests that even unwritten idol names may be mentioned.

keyTerms.meaning: A man fully impure because of discharges
From גדיון to שילה, a measure of distance; גדיון is an idol's name

phrases.english: And if it is not written – it is not permitted?
רב משרשיא raises an objection:
phrases.notes: He quotes a משנה in זבים 1:5.

phrases.english: If he saw one discharge as long as three,
which is like the time from גדיון to שילה,
phrases.notes: גדיון is the name of an idol. That is the whole point of the challenge.

phrases.english: which is the time of two immersions and two dryings –
he is a full-fledged זב.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא כְּתִיבָא – לָא? מֵתִיב רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the implied flip side of רבי יוחנן's rule from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that unwritten idol names may not be mentioned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה freely names גדיון, which seems to be an unwritten idol, so unwritten names must also be allowed.

steps.title: רבינא: גד is also written
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the idol גד is also written in a פסוק, so the משנה was allowed to say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: גד is also written, as it is written: 'Who set a table for גד.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends רבי יוחנן's rule by showing that the idol in the משנה is written after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גדיון is a form of the idol גד, and גד appears in ישעיהו. So the משנה fits רבי יוחנן's rule, and the limit to written names stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of an idol, the root of the name גדיון

steps.whatToRemember: An idol's name may be mentioned only if it appears in תנ״ך. נבו and גד both appear in ישעיהו.

phrases.english: רבינא said:
גד is also actually written,
as it is written: "Who set a table for גד."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 65:11

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: גַּד נָמֵי מִכְתָּב כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב משרשיא's objection from step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the case in the משנה is really a written name.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: גדיון is an unwritten idol name, so the משנה shows unwritten names are allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: גד is written in ישעיהו, so the משנה fits רבי יוחנן's rule.

steps.title: רב נחמן: mocking idols is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that all mockery is forbidden except mockery of עבודה זרה, and proves it from a פסוק that ridicules בל and נבו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: All mockery is forbidden, except mockery of idol worship, which is permitted, as it is written: 'בל bows down, נבו stoops... they stoop, they bow down together, they could not hold back the burden.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רב נחמן. Making fun of things is forbidden, but making fun of idols is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is that the נביא himself mocks the idols. He shows them crouching helplessly and unable to hold back their 'burden'. If the פסוק ridicules idols this way, we may do it too.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule. Joking and mockery are normally forbidden, but ridiculing עבודה זרה is an exception.

phrases.english: רב נחמן said:
All mockery is forbidden,
except for mockery of idol worship, which is permitted,
as it is written: "Bel bows down, נבו stoops...
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 46:1-2. The dots mean the גמרא skips some words in the middle of the פסוק.

phrases.english: they stoop, they bow down together,
they could not hold back the burden."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: כֹּל לֵיצָנוּתָא אֲסִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new rule. It uses the same פסוק about בל and נבו from step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All mockery is forbidden except mockery of עבודה זרה, which is permitted.

steps.title: A second פסוק: read 'its burden' instead of 'its glory'
steps.stepSummary: A second proof from הושע: the פסוק says the idol's 'glory' has gone, but the גמרא reads it as its 'burden', which is another insult to the idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'They speak... the people of שומרון will fear for the calves of בית און, for its people mourn over it and its priests tremble for it, for its glory, because it has gone from it.' Do not read 'its glory' (כבודו), but 'its burden' (כבידו).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second פסוק to support רב נחמן's rule that mocking idols is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By changing כבודו (its glory) to כבידו (its burden), the גמרא turns the פסוק into a crude insult to the calf idol. This matches the 'burden' language of the first פסוק. It shows again that תנ״ך itself mocks idols.

keyTerms.meaning: The calf idols of בית און, a mocking name for בית אל
Do not read it as; a way of rereading a word in a פסוק
Its burden or heaviness, in place of כבודו, its glory

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's rule: mocking עבודה זרה is the one kind of mockery that is allowed, and two פסוקים prove it (ישעיהו and הושע).

phrases.english: And it is written: "They speak...
phrases.notes: הושע 10:4-5. The dots mean the גמרא skips words between the two פסוקים.

phrases.aramaic: לְעֶגְלוֹת בֵּית אָוֶן יָגוּרוּ שְׁכַן שֹׁמְרוֹן
phrases.english: the people of שומרון will be in fear for the calves of בית און;
for its people mourn over it,
and its priests tremble over it,
for its glory, because it has gone away from it."
Do not read "its glory" (כבודו), but rather "its burden" (כבידו).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק to support רב נחמן's rule in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's rule that mocking עבודה זרה is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: הושע 10:5, reread as כבידו, so the פסוק itself mocks the calf idol

steps.title: Everyone carried a little idol in his pocket
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains the words כתבונם עצבים in הושע to mean that each person made a small image of his god, kept it in his pocket, and hugged and kissed it whenever he thought of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק says: What does the פסוק mean: 'And now they continue to sin, and have made for themselves molten images of their silver, according to their understanding, idols'? What is 'according to their understanding, idols'? It teaches that each person made an image of his god and put it in his pocket. Whenever he remembered it, he took it out of his bosom and hugged it and kissed it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק explains a פסוק in הושע. It shows how silly and personal idol worship had become: people carried pocket idols and kissed them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is כתבונם. רבי יצחק reads it as describing a personal, pocket-sized image, so each person had his own little god. Following רב נחמן's rule in step 19, this is the kind of mocking of עבודה זרה the פסוקים themselves do.

keyTerms.meaning: Usually 'according to their understanding'; here read as describing each person's own image of his god
Literally 'what he fears', meaning his god
His bosom, the fold of his garment near his chest

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak says:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"And now they continue to sin,
phrases.notes: הושע 13:2

phrases.english: and have made for themselves molten images of their silver,
according to their understanding, idols, etc."
What is "according to their understanding, idols"?
It teaches that each and every one
would make an image of his god
and place it in his pocket.
When he would remember it,
he would take it out of his bosom
and hug it and kiss it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another explanation of a פסוק in הושע that mocks idol worship, continuing the theme of steps 19-20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כתבונם עצבים teaches that each person carried a personal idol in his pocket and hugged and kissed it.

steps.title: What does 'those who sacrifice men kiss calves' mean
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the last words of the same פסוק: 'those who sacrifice men kiss calves.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'those who sacrifice men kiss calves'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking about the end of the same פסוק in הושע. Two answers will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are puzzling: who sacrifices people, and why do calves get kissed? The question opens a small discussion where רבי יצחק דבי רבי אמי and רבא give different readings.

keyTerms.meaning: Calves, here calves that were worshipped as idols
They kiss (or: are made to kiss)

phrases.english: What is the meaning of "those who sacrifice men kiss calves"?
phrases.notes: These are the closing words of the same פסוק, הושע 13:2.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first half of the פסוק (step 21) to its last words.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase זובחי אדם עגלים ישקון.

steps.title: The priests' trick to get rich men sacrificed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק דבי רבי אמי explains that idol priests starved the calves next to statues of rich men. When the hungry calves ran to the real rich men, the priests said the idol wanted him to sacrifice himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק דבי רבי אמי says: The idol priests would set their eyes on rich people. They would starve the calves, make statues that looked like those rich men, and stand them next to the calves' feeding troughs. Then they took the calves outside. When the calves saw those men, they ran after them and pawed at them. The priests would say to the man: The idol wants you; come and sacrifice yourself to it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק דבי רבי אמי answers the question. He says the פסוק describes a trick: priests made calves 'choose' rich men so that those men would be sacrificed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The calves learned to link the rich man's face with food, so they ran to him when hungry. The priests used this to say the idol 'desired' him. In this reading the kissing calves are a tool to get people sacrificed.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not get mixed up about who is who. 'Them' sometimes means the calves and sometimes the rich men. The calves run after the rich men, and the priests are the ones talking.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק דְּבֵי רַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak of the school of Rabbi Ami says:
That the idol priests
would set their eyes on wealthy people,
and starve the calves,
and make statues in their image,
phrases.notes: The statues were made to look like those rich men.

phrases.english: and stand them next to their feeding troughs,
and take them (the calves) outside.
Once they (the calves) saw them (the rich men),
they would run after them and paw at them.
They (the priests) would say to him:
The idol desires you;
let him come and sacrifice himself to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק דְּבֵי רַבִּי אַמֵּי: שֶׁהָיוּ כּוֹמָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The calves 'kiss' (paw) rich men because of the priests' trick, which leads to those men being sacrificed.

steps.title: רבא: the wording does not fit that reading
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the previous explanation. If it were right, the פסוק should have said 'calves are made to kiss in order to sacrifice men.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: Is this what 'those who sacrifice men kiss calves' means? It should have said: 'Calves are made to kiss in order to sacrifice men'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on the answer of רבי יצחק דבי רבי אמי. The order of the words in the פסוק does not match that story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the story the calves' kissing comes first and causes the sacrifice. But the פסוק starts with 'those who sacrifice men' as the ones doing the kissing. So the wording points to people who already sacrificed and then kiss calves.

keyTerms.meaning: In order to sacrifice a person

phrases.english: Rava says:
Is this "those who sacrifice men kiss calves"?
"Calves are made to kiss in order to sacrifice men"
it should have said!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי ״זֹבְחֵי אָדָם עֲגָלִים יִשָּׁקוּן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the explanation given in step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole reading of רבי יצחק דבי רבי אמי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word order of the פסוק puts the sacrificers as the subject who kiss, not the calves kissing so that men will be sacrificed.

steps.title: רבא: the reward for sacrificing a son is kissing the calf
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives his own reading: whoever sacrificed his son to an idol was told he gave a great gift, so he earned the right to come and kiss the calf.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא says: Anyone who sacrifices his son to idol worship, the priest says to him: You have offered a great gift to it; come and kiss it.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the first reading, רבא explains the phrase in a way that fits the word order. 'Those who sacrifice men' are the ones who then get to 'kiss calves.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the people who sacrifice come first, just like the פסוק. Their 'reward' for the terrible act of killing a child is only to kiss a calf. This shows how empty and foolish idol worship is.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of 'those who sacrifice men kiss calves': a priests' trick that leads rich men to be sacrificed, or רבא's reading, where kissing the calf is the reward for sacrificing a son. רבא prefers his because it fits the word order.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַזּוֹבֵחַ אֶת בְּנוֹ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
phrases.english: Anyone who sacrifices his son to idol worship,
(the priest) says to him:
He has offered a great gift to it;
let him come and kiss it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: כׇּל הַזּוֹבֵחַ אֶת בְּנוֹ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reading rejected in step 24 with a new one that fits the wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זובחי אדם עגלים ישקון means that those who sacrificed a child were 'rewarded' by being allowed to kiss the idol calf.

steps.title: The animal shapes of the idols of the nations in שומרון
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב explains the idols named in מלכים ב: סכות בנות was a hen, נרגל a rooster, אשימא a bald goat, and נבחן and תרתק a dog and a donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה says in the name of רב: 'And the men of בבל made סכות בנות.' What is it? A hen. 'And the men of כות made נרגל.' What is it? A rooster. 'And the men of חמת made אשימא.' What is it? A bald goat. 'And the עוים made נבחן and תרתק.' What are they? A dog and a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: רב goes through the list of idols that the nations brought to שומרון and says what each one looked like. Each one turns out to be a plain animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying that these grand-sounding idols were just a hen, a rooster, a goat, a dog and a donkey shows how silly they were. This fits רב נחמן's rule (step 19) that mocking עבודה זרה is allowed.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says that Rav says:
"And the men of Babylonia made Succoth-Benoth";
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 17:30, about the nations the Assyrians settled in שומרון.

phrases.english: and what is it? A hen.
"And the men of Cuth made Nergal";
and what is it? A rooster.
"And the men of Hamath made Ashima";
and what is it? A bald billy goat.
"And the Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak";
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 17:31

phrases.english: and what are they? A dog and a donkey.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: ״וְאַנְשֵׁי בָבֶל עָשׂוּ אֶת סֻכּוֹת בְּנוֹת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from הושע to a new list of idols in מלכים ב, still on the theme of making idol worship look foolish.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The idols סכות בנות, נרגל, אשימא, נבחן and תרתק were shaped like a hen, a rooster, a bald goat, a dog and a donkey.

steps.title: The gods of ספרוים: the mule and the horse
steps.stepSummary: Continuing רב's list, the גמרא identifies אדרמלך and ענמלך as the mule and the horse, and explains each name.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And the people of ספרוים burned their sons and daughters in fire to אדרמלך and ענמלך, the gods of ספרוים." What were these? The mule and the horse. The mule is called אדרמלך because it honors its master by carrying his load. The horse is called ענמלך because it answers its master in battle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going with רב's list of idols from מלכים ב. It names the last two idols and explains why they were called by those names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each name is broken into a meaningful word plus מלך (king or master). אדר means honor, which fits the mule that carries its master's load. ענה means answer, which fits the horse that serves its master in war.

keyTerms.meaning: An idol of ספרוים, identified as the mule
An idol of ספרוים, identified as the horse

phrases.english: "And the Sepharvites burned their sons
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 17:31

phrases.english: and their daughters in the fire
to Adrammelech and Anammelech,
the gods of Sepharvaim";
and what are they?
The mule and the horse.
Adrammelech, because it honors its master with its load,
phrases.notes: The mule is the one that carries its owner's packages, so it "honors" him by doing the hauling.

phrases.english: and Anammelech, because it answers its master in battle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of idols from מלכים ב begun by רב יהודה in the name of רב in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אדרמלך is the mule, which carries its master's load, and ענמלך is the horse, which serves its master in battle.

steps.title: חזקיה is saved from being burned
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה's father tried to burn him to an idol, but his mother smeared him with salamander so the fire would not harm him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even חזקיה king of יהודה: his father wanted to do this to him, but his mother smeared him with salamander.
steps.whatsHappening: The verse just quoted spoke about burning children to idols. Now the גמרא adds a story that this nearly happened to חזקיה himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "כן" (so) ties the story to the practice in the פסוק, burning a child to an idol. His mother protected him with the salamander, a creature thought to be fireproof.

keyTerms.meaning: Salamander, a creature believed to be immune to fire

phrases.english: Even Hezekiah, king of Judea:
his father tried to do so to him,
phrases.notes: "So" means burning him in fire to an idol, like the practice in the פסוק just quoted.

phrases.english: but his mother smeared him with salamander.
phrases.notes: The salamander was believed to be fireproof, so smearing him with it kept the flames from burning him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף חִזְקִיָּה מֶלֶךְ יְהוּדָה בִּיקֵּשׁ אָבִיו לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a story about burning children, the practice described in the פסוק of step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיה was almost burned to an idol by his father but was saved by his mother's salamander.

steps.title: Israel knew idols were empty but used them to permit immorality
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב says that Israel knew idols had no real power. They worshipped them only as an excuse to commit עריות openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Israel knew that idol worship has nothing real to it. They worshipped idols only to permit themselves forbidden relations in public.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins. רב claims that Israel's idol worship was never real belief. It was a cover for public immorality.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב separates what Israel believed from what they did. They did not think the idols had power. They wanted the immoral freedom that came with idol rituals.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next challenge, which will test whether Israel really had no emotional attachment to idols.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The Jewish people knew about idol worship
that there is no substance in it,
and they did not worship idols
except to permit themselves forbidden relations in public.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: יוֹדְעִין הָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about Israel's motive for idol worship.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Israel did not believe in idols. They worshipped them only to allow open immorality.

steps.title: Challenge: Israel longed for idols like a parent misses a child
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא challenges רב using a פסוק in ירמיהו and רבי אלעזר's reading of it, which shows Israel truly loved their idols.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא objected: "Like remembering their sons are their altars..." And רבי אלעזר said this means like a person who longs for his son.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא attacks רב's statement. He quotes a פסוק and a דרשה showing that Israel missed their idols deeply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If Israel only used idols as an excuse, they would not long for them. רבי אלעזר compares their longing to a parent missing a child, which shows real emotional attachment and contradicts רב. The next step answers this.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya raises an objection:
"Like the memory of their sons are their altars, etc."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 17:2

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּאָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ גַּעְגּוּעִין עַל בְּנוֹ?
phrases.english: like a person who longs for his son?
phrases.notes: Longing like that means they really cared about the idols, which does not fit רב's idea that it was all an excuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רב's claim in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that Israel knew idols were empty and worshipped them only for immorality.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר reads the פסוק as Israel longing for their altars like a parent misses a child. That kind of longing shows real attachment to idols, not just an excuse.

steps.title: They loved the idols only after becoming attached to them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers רב משרשיא's challenge. The love for idols described in ירמיהו came only after ישראל had become attached to idol worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: That was only after they became attached to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב against רב משרשיא's challenge. It says the deep love for idols came later, only after ישראל got attached to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said ישראל worshipped idols only as an excuse for עריות. The פסוק in ירמיהו shows real love for idols. The answer splits this into two stages: at first it was only an excuse, and later, once they were hooked, they truly came to love the idols.

keyTerms.meaning: That they became attached to it, meaning they got 'stuck' to idol worship

phrases.english: After they became attached to it.
phrases.notes: 'It' means idol worship. At the start it was only about the עריות, and the real love came later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רב משרשיא's challenge from step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the time period: an early stage and a later stage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק in ירמיהו shows ישראל loved idols, which contradicts רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are true at different times. First the idols were an excuse for עריות, and later ישראל grew attached to them and loved them.

steps.title: A new proof: the פסוק about carcasses and אליהו finding a starving child
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new source to test רב's claim. It begins with a פסוק about 'carcasses on carcasses of your idols' and a story of אליהו הצדיק finding a swollen, starving child in the garbage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And I will place your carcasses upon the carcasses of your idols.' They said: אליהו הצדיק used to go around looking for people swollen from hunger in ירושלים. Once he found a child who was swollen and lying in a garbage heap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge to רב with 'come and hear'. It is setting up a story that will show how much ישראל were attached to their idols.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'come and hear' signals that this source will be used against רב's view that the idols were only an excuse. The story is not finished yet. Its point, that people truly clung to their idols, comes in the next part of the story.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"And I will place your carcasses upon the carcasses of your idols."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 26:30

phrases.english: It was said: Elijah the righteous

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה מְחַזֵּר עַל תְּפוּחֵי רָעָב שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלַיִם.
phrases.english: used to go around looking for those swollen from hunger in Jerusalem.
phrases.notes: Starving people's bodies swell up. אליהו was searching for them to help them.

phrases.english: Once he found a child
who was swollen and lying in a garbage heap.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After answering רב משרשיא, the גמרא brings another source that seems to challenge רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim (step 29) that ישראל worshipped idols only as an excuse for עריות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק and the story that follows will show people truly clinging to their idols, which suggests real devotion and not just an excuse.

steps.title: אליהו talks with the child and teaches him שמע ישראל
steps.stepSummary: אליהו asks the child about his family and learns that he is the only one left. He offers to teach him something to live by and tells him to say שמע ישראל every day. The child's reply is about to come.
steps.simpleTranslation: אליהו said to him: Which family are you from? He said: From such-and-such family. אליהו said: Is anyone left from that family? He said: No, except me. אליהו said: If I teach you something you can live by, will you learn it? He said: Yes. אליהו said: Say every day, 'Hear O Israel, ה׳ is our God, ה׳ is One.' The child said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. אליהו offers the dying child a way to live: saying שמע ישראל every day. The section stops just as the child begins to answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole family has died, and only this starving child is left. אליהו offers him life through declaring ה׳'s oneness. The child's answer, which comes next, is the key to how this story proves attachment to idols.

keyTerms.meaning: Such-and-such, a stand-in for a name
Hear O Israel, the declaration of ה׳'s oneness

steps.confusionAlert: The story is not finished here. The child's answer, which carries the point of the proof, comes in the next part, so don't try to draw the conclusion yet.

phrases.english: He said to him: From which family are you?
He said to him: I am from such-and-such family.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: כְּלוּם נִשְׁתַּיֵּיר מֵאוֹתָהּ מִשְׁפָּחָה?
phrases.english: He said to him: Is anyone left from that family?
He said to him: No, except for me.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אִם אֲנִי מְלַמֶּדְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁאַתָּה חַי בּוֹ,
phrases.english: He said to him: If I teach you something by which you will live,
will you learn it?
He said to him: Yes.
He said to him: Say every day
"Hear O Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One."
phrases.notes: דברים 6:4

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is the child starting to answer. His actual words come right after this, in the next part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun in step 32, building toward the child's reply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אליהו offers the last surviving child of a family a way to live: saying שמע ישראל every day.
